content_en: A project team forgot to complete a planned task in an iteration. During a daily coordination meeting 3 days later, the team realized the task was not completed. Later that day, the team completed the task. What should the project manager do to avoid this situation in the future?
option_1_content_en: Examine the issue during the retrospective.
option_2_content_en: Address the issue in the demo.
option_3_content_en: Discuss the issue during the next iteration planning.
option_4_content_en: Send an email to the team.

content_en: A project management office (PMO) wants to offer constant reporting across dozens of agile projects running concurrently. The PMO wants to use information radiators to share progress status and key lessons learned. How can this be achieved?
option_1_content_en: Create dashboards that display combined feature burnup charts and a summary of retrospectives.
option_2_content_en: Place webcams to broadcast all kanban boards and cycle the images sequentially on the information radiator.
option_3_content_en: Use fishbowl windows to show all project team kanban boards and charts in real time.
option_4_content_en: Set up an internal Wiki page for all agile teams to update in real time and for users to consult on demand.

content_en: The last three agile iterations showed a trend of increasingly prolonged test work. Which action should the project manager take to address the root cause of this issue?
option_1_content_en: Discuss this in the next iteration planning meeting.
option_2_content_en: Plan an iteration of testing only.
option_3_content_en: Practice a paired testing policy.
option_4_content_en: Refine the backlog.

content_en: A project team alerted a product owner after three agile iterations showed a trend of increasingly prolonged work. The product owner performed an intensive backlog refinement.Which metric shows the problem was effectively addressed?
option_1_content_en: Increase in value per story
option_2_content_en: Speed of impediment resolution
option_3_content_en: Stories completed per iteration
option_4_content_en: Decrease in backlog item count

content_en: During execution, updated performance data shows that several sustainability initiatives are delivering long-term benefits but are increasing short-term cost and schedule pressure. Stakeholders are divided between protecting near-term commitments and preserving long-term value outcomes. Which actions should the project manager take? (Select all that apply.)
option_1_content_en: Reassess initiative priorities using updated value, cost, and sustainability information.
option_2_content_en: Reduce or pause sustainability initiatives to protect near-term schedule commitments.
option_3_content_en: Communicate trade-offs and value implications to stakeholders to support decisions.
option_4_content_en: Continue executing all initiatives as planned to avoid revisiting prior decisions.
option_5_content_en: Align delivery decisions with agreed value criteria and governance thresholds.

content_en:
The project manager receives the weekly project status report. The report includes a schedule, budget status, and risk updates. A risk has been identified in the last reporting period, and its impact is described as moderate, with mitigation actions underway. The project is behind schedule due to delayed approval on a key deliverable, but the budget is on track. 

Based on the project status report, what should the project manager focus on in the next week to ensure project success?
option_1_content_en: Monitoring the risk and updating the project schedule to reflect realistic timelines
option_2_content_en: Approving additional budget allocation organizationally to resolve the delayed deliverable and prevent further delays
option_3_content_en: Notifying all stakeholders about the schedule delay and requesting a formal change in scope to compensate for lost time
option_4_content_en: Increasing the frequency of risk reporting and concentrating efforts on budget management

content_en: During a meeting, a project manager learns that a business result needs to be delivered in 12 weeks, although the original schedule stated 16 weeks. The project manager also learns the assigned technical specialist is already working on another project. What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Notify the project sponsor about the lack of a technical resource.
option_2_content_en: Immediately escalate the issue to decision-makers in the organization.
option_3_content_en: Raise the issue of not being done in 12 weeks and develop an appropriate response.
option_4_content_en: Hire an outside party to meet the need for a technical resource.

content_en: A project manager is working in a virtual team. During the third iteration of a project to develop a product, the project manager realizes the team dashboard is faulty and not showing updates. Which action should the project manager take next?
option_1_content_en: Send daily team email updates.
option_2_content_en: Rank the need to fix the dashboard according to the business value for upcoming iterations.
option_3_content_en: Fix the dashboard.
option_4_content_en: Document the issue as a new project risk and propose a solution.

content_en: During an iteration, a project team working in country B encounters problems that may cause a delay in the completion of task B. Teams in country A need task B to be completed on time to meet their schedules. These teams work together virtually. What should the project manager do to resolve this problem?
option_1_content_en: Ask the team in country B to work harder to complete on time to avoid delaying the work of other teams.
option_2_content_en: Ask the teams to collaborate virtually to find a solution to avert the potential delay.
option_3_content_en: Increase the iteration length and add additional resources to the project team so they can meet the appropriate deadlines.
option_4_content_en: Ask team members to perform to the best of their abilities during the iteration and engage in a retrospective after completion of the iteration.

content_en: A long-standing key team member in a virtual team has been unmotivated for weeks following the death of a family member. Several project activities are behind schedule, impacting the critical path of the project. How should the project manager handle this situation?
option_1_content_en: Replace the team member.
option_2_content_en: Work with the team member to identify a workable solution.
option_3_content_en: Escalate this situation as a human resource issue and ask other team members to work overtime.
option_4_content_en: Ask the functional manager for additional support on the project, including adding a new team member.

content_en: A project manager is working on multiple projects. One project has new team members and is in its early stages. The other projects are in various states of execution for the following few weeks. How should the project manager develop the new project team over the following few weeks?
option_1_content_en: Help team members create a set of agreed-on rules for working that encourage team cohesion.
option_2_content_en: Ask team members to engage in multiple team-building events to normalize the team.
option_3_content_en: Keep the team informed by sending short daily project status updates.
option_4_content_en: Engage in face-to-face personal conversations with each team member to build relationships.

content_en: An agile team excels in solving technical problems, but when the product owner requests creative or business-related ideas, the team is silent. Is this a problem?
option_1_content_en: Yes, specialist teams are prone to higher error rates.
option_2_content_en: No, specialist teams are more effective than generalists.
option_3_content_en: Yes, lack of diversity will limit the team's adaptability.
option_4_content_en: No, the team performs better without distractions.

content_en: Match each risk response with its primary purpose.
option_1_content_en: Reduce the probability or impact of a risk
option_2_content_en: Shift risk ownership to a third party
option_3_content_en: Take no immediate action beyond monitoring
option_4_content_en: Eliminate the threat entirely

content_en: A company has hired an architectural excellence board with a mission to implement companywide programming architectures. The agile team, under the supervision of a project manager, continues to work on new and existing software products. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Inform the agile team that resulting changes will be postponed as long as possible.
option_2_content_en: Be patient and wait until the board gives the team explicit instructions, then decide.
option_3_content_en: Speak with the product owner and development team about how this change affects the backlog.
option_4_content_en: Negotiate with the board to protect the team from disruption while making the team aware of organizational changes.

content_en: A project manager observes that team members are feeling down after demos. Feedback from stakeholders is a constant concern for the team. As a result, the team rushes through product demos, and the interaction between the team and stakeholders is minimal. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Meet with the stakeholders to find the root cause of their feedback, then work with them to rectify the problems.
option_2_content_en: Verify that project requirements are suitable and team members can do the work.
option_3_content_en: Coach the team to be more confident in their work and communicate more effectively with the stakeholders.
option_4_content_en: Consult the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix.

content_en: A project team is working with an overseas contractor based in a country with three official languages. Every contractor on the team is multilingual, but the project team speaks only one of those languages. Team meetings continue to be held in the commonly shared language, but during project work meetings contractors speak with one another in a different language. When the project manager raises this issue in the following team meeting, the contractors express regret but explain they work better when they can communicate freely with one another. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Require everyone to speak the same language all of the time, even though this will slow the pace of work.
option_2_content_en: Escalate this as an issue to the human resources department.
option_3_content_en: Obtain formal training or translation services.
option_4_content_en: Let the team discuss language requirements and make ground rules for team communication.

content_en: A team decides a hybrid approach using an iterative development approach fits the needs of the next phase in their project. Unfortunately, some team members do not have experience with iterative development. How should the project manager prepare this team for the next phase?
option_1_content_en: Transition some of these team members to other teams and replace them with agile-trained team members.
option_2_content_en: Help ensure the project's contingency reserve can cover training for all team members.
option_3_content_en: Create virtual training sessions for key team members, covering the main agile topics.
option_4_content_en: Identify and implement training in iterative development for the team members.

content_en: A project team has been efficiently delivering results on a product upgrade. The upgrade must be released in 3 months or a competitor’s new product will make theirs obsolete. Citing this reason, the product owner suddenly requests a feature revision; however, no one on the project team can do the work. The project sponsor is willing to extend the budget but cannot extend the schedule. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Meet the new demand by adding new team members.
option_2_content_en: Recommend suspending the project until a firm decision can be made.
option_3_content_en: Discuss options with the project owner and choose the best one.
option_4_content_en: Challenge the request and initiate customer research to determine if the new feature is desirable.

content_en: A project team has decided to adopt some agile practices during the final phase in a project. As the team discusses the phase, some team members disclose they have never worked with agile practices. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: File a change request that addresses the agile training that team members lack.
option_2_content_en: Escalate this as an issue to the project sponsor, as it is a companywide issue and a blocker for this project.
option_3_content_en: Ask the team members who have worked with agile to mentor the others.
option_4_content_en: Identify and provide agile training for team members.

content_en: A project has the following characteristics: 1) Schedule performance issues occur due to the low expertise levels of project team members. 2) Junior-level team members are not completing tasks in a timely manner. 3) Highly experienced project team members report that their junior colleagues are performing unnecessary tasks. Which two actions can the project manager take to enhance the performance of this project team? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Meet with the team lead to discuss the situation and decide if escalation to the project sponsor is necessary.
option_2_content_en: Implement a whole-team training program to address efficient working and task completion.
option_3_content_en: Work collaboratively with the project team to design training and a checklist for task completion aligned with project goals.
option_4_content_en: Focus the junior project team members on the more basic tasks to boost overall team performance.
option_5_content_en: Schedule meetings with junior-level and senior-level project team members to determine what is causing project team members to not complete tasks.

content_en: A project manager provided training for the entire project team on new company processes during the kickoff phase of a project. One year later, project productivity is suffering because team members who were added later in the project do not have the same level of understanding. How should the project manager respond to this challenge?
option_1_content_en: Instruct the newer team members to ask the long-term members for help when they do not understand something.
option_2_content_en: Hold an onboarding session with the new team members and ask experienced team members to act as mentors.
option_3_content_en: Add new team members with the relevant experience, reassign the newer team members to other projects, and record turnover issues in the lessons learned register.
option_4_content_en: Recognize that this is a natural project progression and revise the schedule to allow for the slight decrease in productivity.

content_en: Following are the characteristics of a technology development project: The project requires a highly skilled team member who is unavailable locally. The project manager has identified a team member who can do the work, but the team member lives in a different country and requires a work visa. The work visa process is taking longer than anticipated. What should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Assign overtime work to the existing team.
option_2_content_en: Seek another qualified team member.
option_3_content_en: Delay the project by an equivalent duration.
option_4_content_en: Ask the team member to work remotely.

content_en: A key project team member is asked to move to another project during the middle of a technical project. The team is very concerned because there is no one available with this unique skill set. What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Discuss the conflict with the project sponsor and formulate a response.
option_2_content_en: Use coaching tools and techniques to motivate the project team.
option_3_content_en: Replace the key team member with external talent who has the same skills.
option_4_content_en: Acknowledge the team's concern and analyze the impact to the project.

content_en: A project manager is working on a small project that is critical for a larger program milestone. A new team member has been assigned to replace a key team member who left the project. A stakeholder claims the new team member has a disruptive approach to work. What should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Ask the project team what they think about the new colleague's performance and task delivery.
option_2_content_en: Meet with the new team member to understand their approach and how they can align with the project and project team.
option_3_content_en: File a request with the project management office manager to obtain another team member.
option_4_content_en: Approach the new team member's functional manager to help mitigate any conflict within the project team.

content_en: On a project team, staff members from various organizational departments rotate in and out, to augment the team. How can the project manager maintain high team performance?
option_1_content_en: Allow nonrotating project team members to assign tasks to the rotating members.
option_2_content_en: Implement a training program so rotating team members can share their skills.
option_3_content_en: Give the nonrotating project team members higher priority to choose which tasks they work on.
option_4_content_en: Require project team members leaving the project to document their knowledge in lessons learned.

content_en: A project manager replaces a retiring project manager on a project team. During initial meetings, the project manager realized the team members disagree about how to address technical decisions. Team members did not respect one another's ideas, and the environment was becoming counterproductive. With the new project manager’s leadership, however, the team has begun to communicate more effectively and develop some processes and procedures for working together. In what phase of development is the project team now?
option_1_content_en: Forming
option_2_content_en: Storming
option_3_content_en: Norming
option_4_content_en: People

content_en: An unresolved conflict between a member of a third-party vendor's team and a member of a project team is causing disruption. What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Meet with the vendor to discuss the situation.
option_2_content_en: Place this item in the issue log.
option_3_content_en: Draft and send a contractual letter to the vendor.
option_4_content_en: Coach the internal team member.

content_en: A project team consists of local and virtual team members. To manage scheduling priority conflicts among team members, the project manager schedules a videoconference call to find an agreed-on solution to the conflicts. Which conflict resolution technique does this statement demonstrate?
option_1_content_en: Smooth/accommodate
option_2_content_en: Collaborate/problem-solve
option_3_content_en: Force/direct
option_4_content_en: Compromise/reconcile

content_en: During an iteration review, a few key stakeholders do not approve of the implementation of a user story. What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Invite project team members to a brainstorming session to identify an appropriate response.
option_2_content_en: Learn why the stakeholders are concerned.
option_3_content_en: Determine the impact of the conflict by listing the pros and cons of the situation.
option_4_content_en: Ask the project sponsor to act as a neutral party in negotiation with the dissatisfied stakeholders.

content_en: At a weekly project status meeting, a key team member expresses concern about the overall approach documented in the project management plan. The project manager is surprised, because the team is in the process of executing an important component of the project and the concern has not been raised before. Which steps should the project manager take?
option_1_content_en: Update the issue log to document the concerns, then continue with the meeting's scheduled agenda items.
option_2_content_en: Recognize that the concern must be discussed and resolved prior to continuing with the meeting's agenda items.
option_3_content_en: Address the team with a generic reminder about meeting etiquette, then ask if the team wants to use the time to discuss the concerns raised during the meeting.
option_4_content_en: Acknowledge the team member's concern immediately, continue with the scheduled agenda, then meet with the team member to understand their concerns.

content_en: A research and development executive—who is a project stakeholder—occasionally visits an agile team's work area, and instruct them to work on features he feels are more urgent. The team accepts the instructions and begins work. During iteration reviews, the product owner becomes upset that the team worked on the requested features. Which two actions should the project team take to address the problem? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor to help ensure the executive no longer interferes with the team.
option_2_content_en: Meet with the product owner to make adjustments for working with the stakeholder.
option_3_content_en: Stop doing work prioritized by the research and development executive.
option_4_content_en: Instruct the executive to communicate directly with the product owner about any inputs.
option_5_content_en: Provide the executive with access to add new items to the backlog.

content_en: A hybrid development team changes a design element in a project while the product owner is on vacation. Testing results improve dramatically over the next two iterations. During the third iteration review, the product owner is unhappy to learn about the change to the original design and asks the project team to redo the work based on the original design. How should the project manager get the project back on track?
option_1_content_en: Set out all decision path conditions in the ground rules and correct any deviations as early as possible.
option_2_content_en: Request additional funding from the product owner for rework due to lack of collaboration with the team.
option_3_content_en: Work with the product owner to prioritize the fix in the next iteration.
option_4_content_en: As servant leader, help the team to focus by removing all impediments.

content_en: Project team members are concerned that a new team member does not seem suitable for an assigned task because their work is introducing errors. The project manager gathers some initial data about the team member's work. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Contact senior management to discuss the possibility of reassigning the new team member to a different project.
option_2_content_en: Schedule time to chat with the new team member to reassess their skills and understand their challenges.
option_3_content_en: Ask the team members to document task-related deficiencies displayed by the new team member.
option_4_content_en: Contact the project sponsor to highlight these concerns and decide on an appropriate response.

content_en: A project manager notices a team member is not making progress on a key activity. During a face-to-face meeting, the team member says they feel they are not in the correct role within the project team. What should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Reassure the team member about their abilities by reminding them that they were chosen for a reason.
option_2_content_en: Ask the team member why they feel they are not in the correct role.
option_3_content_en: Enroll the team member in targeted training to acquire the needed skills for their assigned role.
option_4_content_en: Reassign the team member to a more appropriate role in another project.

content_en: During a product review at the end of an iteration, a customer asks the project team to change their technical approach for a product in development. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Work with team members to immediately implement the new approach.
option_2_content_en: Help ensure they understand why the customer is asking for the change and conduct an optional spike to determine viability.
option_3_content_en: Discuss the pros and cons of the proposed approach with stakeholders, then select the approach that is best for the team and notify team members.
option_4_content_en: Allow the team to benchmark the approach to obtain sponsor buy-in.

content_en: A project manager outsources project work to overseas contractors so they can work remotely on the user stories. In their first iteration, the overseas team did not understand specific usability requirements because of cultural references in the user stories. Despite this, the team completed five user stories that were previously blocked because the original team could not handle the algorithmic complexity of the work. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Engage an interpreter to translate all the requirements.
option_2_content_en: Assign all the user stories to local team members.
option_3_content_en: Ask the product owner to reprioritize the backlog to match the remote team's skills.
option_4_content_en: Find another remote team with better linguistic skills.

content_en: A recently formed agile team is exhausted after working 12-hour days to fulfill sprint commitments. Who has not properly performed their duties in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Project manager
option_2_content_en: Team members
option_3_content_en: Product owner
option_4_content_en: Scrum master

content_en: A project manager is preparing a project charter. The project goal is to automate 30% of the company’s product testing. The project sponsor advises the project manager to assign senior test engineers to identify the tests that can be automated. The test department manager, however, is not cooperative because they believe the project will lead to downsizing in their department. Which two actions should the project manager take in this scenario? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Ask the project sponsor to provide a rationale for test automation.
option_2_content_en: Present the test department manager with data-driven, cost-benefit evidence of test automation.
option_3_content_en: Raise the risk that the senior testing engineers will not be available for the testing.
option_4_content_en: Work with the project sponsor to create a project charter that the test department manager will not perceive as threatening.
option_5_content_en: Ask the test department manager to assign someone from their team to assist with the automation.

content_en: A customer is not satisfied with a delivered product because it was not what they expected. The project manager is surprised, because the agile development team delivered several iterations of the product early. What should the project manager do to resolve the situation?
option_1_content_en: Require team sign off for each of the changes to the requirements.
option_2_content_en: Allocate more resources for product testing after making changes.
option_3_content_en: Explain to the customer the value of demos and the approval process followed for the deliverable.
option_4_content_en: Help ensure the development team fully participated in the iteration review by explaining their solutions and answering questions.

content_en: During the planning stage of a project in a matrix organization, a project manager identifies the number and types of team members required to complete the work. Because of an ongoing change management initiative, the functional managers report that planned resources and personnel are not available for the project. The project manager is unsure about the project. Which two steps should the project manager take next? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Collaborate with the customer to renegotiate timelines or budget to enable resource planning.
option_2_content_en: Determine the project's most critical priorities and focus on delivering those supported by available team members and resources.
option_3_content_en: Investigate options for procuring or otherwise obtaining the required team members and resources.
option_4_content_en: Help ensure the impact of the shortage of required resources is fully documented.
option_5_content_en: Reevaluate the project objectives, review the planned activities, and recalculate the team member and resource needs.

content_en: Project deliverables should be reviewed for quality and pass a series of quality tests that have just been introduced through an updated organizational quality policy. The quality manager is concerned because a high proportion of the deliverables are failing early quality tests. What should the project manager do first to help ensure the project can continue successfully?
option_1_content_en: Generate a cause-and-effect diagram for analysis.
option_2_content_en: Determine whether the new process or the product is faulty.
option_3_content_en: Conduct an internal audit of the project.
option_4_content_en: Request advice from a subject matter expert.

content_en: A project sponsor needs to be certain that specific product features will be ready for mass production by a specific date. Which two characteristics of agile development approaches can fulfill the project sponsor’s request? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Incremental delivery mitigates the risk of missing the deadline.
option_2_content_en: User stories are prioritized for each iteration.
option_3_content_en: Incremental development reduces the risk of delays because of quality.
option_4_content_en: Impact mapping can be used to group related stories.
option_5_content_en: Product mapping can be used to prioritize specific product features.

content_en: A hybrid project team needs to deliver a product with a challenging timeline. The product owner recently learned that key stakeholders are worried that the current release plan will not meet urgent business needs. How should the stakeholder concerns be addressed?
option_1_content_en: The project manager can renegotiate the scope with the project sponsor after examining the backlog.
option_2_content_en: The project team can consult with the product owner to identify the minimum viable product (MVP) needed for launch.
option_3_content_en: The project team and product owner can collaborate on incremental product development.
option_4_content_en: The project team should monitor progress using a burndown chart.

content_en: A stakeholder with a minor role in a project wants to add an untested functionality to a product during the execution stage. The project manager determines that the cost for the addition would be small but the additional functionality, if successful, would increase the opportunity for financial profit.  What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Reject the request because it is out of scope.
option_2_content_en: Submit a change request.
option_3_content_en: Evaluate the risk of the requested functionality.
option_4_content_en: Propose a tested alternative.

content_en: During a daily scrum, team members express frustration with the amount of rework on a project. The performance metrics show the team works at a consistent velocity. Which two actions should the scrum master take? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Resolve the technical debt on the project.
option_2_content_en: Ask team members to implement a spike.
option_3_content_en: Add a team member to assist with repetitive work.
option_4_content_en: Investigate the quality process linked to the acceptance criteria.
option_5_content_en: Refine the definition of done (DoD).

content_en: A travel company wants to create an app for their customers. Competitors are racing to do the same, so the app is the company’s highest priority. The product owner’s vision describes several versions of the app—from most basic to premium options. How should the company proceed?
option_1_content_en: Authorize an agile project to innovate and plan design options.
option_2_content_en: Create clear requirements for each potential version of the product and use iterative development.
option_3_content_en: Build a business case for the initiative.
option_4_content_en: Develop a minimum viable product (MVP) and then build incrementally.

content_en: An agile team in a small IT company has been asked to design a new product for the company’s portfolio. The team delivers a list of potential product ideas to the portfolio owner, who responds very positively. Leadership likes two of the product ideas. What should the agile team expect to happen next?
option_1_content_en: A program will be initiated for the product offering.
option_2_content_en: The business case for the products will be put forward for approval.
option_3_content_en: The portfolio owner, as the project sponsor, will authorize a project.
option_4_content_en: A product owner will be assigned to work with the team.

content_en: A risk register excerpt shows several identified project risks, with one marked as both “high impact” and “high probability.” The mitigation action suggested is to hire additional resources to speed up the tasks related to this risk. What action should the project manager take in response to this identified risk?
option_1_content_en: Immediately approve the hiring of additional resources strategically to mitigate the risk and minimize the potential impact.
option_2_content_en: Update the risk response strategy to include contingency planning for alternative mitigation actions.
option_3_content_en: Request further analysis from the team to determine whether additional resources are necessary, given the project's constraints.
option_4_content_en: Reassign current team members to prioritize the identified risk, while postponing noncritical tasks.

content_en: A marketing director wants to be first to market on a mobile e-commerce app for older adults. The marketing director asks an agile team to develop the app. What should the agile team do next?
option_1_content_en: Work with the product owner and subject matter experts (SMEs) to break the requirements down into user stories.
option_2_content_en: Meet with the product owner, agile team, and SMEs to identify risks and risk responses.
option_3_content_en: Ask the team to estimate the effort and build the business case accordingly.
option_4_content_en: Meet with the product owner, agile team, and SMEs to define the minimum viable product (MVP).

content_en: A company is losing market share to competitors with new business models. The agile team in the company has been asked to restrict the number of features of a product and release a version onto the market more quickly. What should the project team and product owner do next?
option_1_content_en: Prioritize the product backlog to develop competitive features in increments for the next release.
option_2_content_en: Update the product vision to reflect a user-driven release roadmap.
option_3_content_en: Reprioritize the product backlog so work is done on the smallest and simplest stories first.
option_4_content_en: Reduce the length of future iterations to enable more feedback and faster product releases.

content_en: A project team in a small company is executing a project. The customer wants to add a few new product features to a project deliverable. Which step should the project manager take first before working on these new product features?

Case Study 1: Enterprise Transformation and Strategic Alignment

A midsized, multinational organization is launching a strategic transformation initiative aimed at improving cross-functional collaboration and accelerating value delivery across its core business units. The initiative is driven by increasing market pressure and inconsistent customer outcomes across regions, which senior leadership believes are limiting the organization’s ability to compete and scale effectively over the long term.

You are assigned as the project manager shortly after the project charter is approved. While executive sponsors agree on the need for transformation, early discussions reveal differing interpretations of what project success means in practice. Some leaders emphasize faster delivery and cost efficiency, while others prioritize customer experience, workforce engagement, and the organization’s ability to sustain improved ways of working beyond the life of the project. These perspectives have not yet been consolidated into a shared understanding of the intended outcomes and value to be delivered.

As the initiative progresses, additional stakeholders become involved, including functional leaders, regional managers, and representatives from operations and support functions. Initial engagement activities take place, but expectations and levels of commitment vary significantly. Some stakeholders actively contribute to defining priorities and success measures, while others remain cautious, expressing concern that the initiative may disrupt existing processes without producing clear, measurable benefits for their areas.

During planning, pressure increases to demonstrate early progress and visible results. Several leaders advocate moving quickly into execution to maintain momentum and stakeholder confidence. At the same time, interdependencies across functions and regions introduce complexity related to governance, sequencing, and coordination. Decisions about the delivery approach and planning practices must balance the desire for speed with the need to maintain alignment to strategic objectives and expected value outcomes.

As execution begins, change requests emerge in response to evolving stakeholder priorities and external influences. While some requests support the original intent of the initiative, others risk shifting focus toward localized optimizations that could dilute overall value and create misalignment across the organization. The project team must determine how changes are assessed, approved, and communicated in a way that preserves strategic alignment, maintains stakeholder trust, and enables informed decision-making.

In the later stages of the initiative, a substantial portion of the planned outcomes has been delivered, and leadership attention starts to move toward new strategic priorities. There is an expectation to formally close the project and transition responsibilities to the organization. However, questions remain about whether the improvements achieved, lessons learned, and enhanced collaboration practices will be embedded into organizational processes and sustained over time, or whether the organization will gradually revert to previous ways of working once the project concludes.

option_1_content_en: Facilitate a structured discussion with key stakeholders to align on the intended outcomes and value as a group.

option_3_content_en: Communicate the transformation objectives broadly to all stakeholders to ensure early awareness and buy-in.
option_4_content_en: Define high-level success metrics based on organizational strategy and circulate them for stakeholder feedback.

content_en: A project team is integrating machine learning (ML) technology into an existing process for medical data analysis used in a project. option_1_content_en: Communications management plan
option_2_content_en: Sprint backlog
option_3_content_en: Definition of ready (DoR)
option_4_content_en: Risk register

content_en: A project manager is working on a small project that is critical for a larger program milestone. A new team member has been assigned to replace a key team member who left the project. A stakeholder claims the new team member has a disruptive approach to work. What should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Review the communications management plan.
option_2_content_en: Review the procurement management plan.
option_3_content_en: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor.
option_4_content_en: Revise the organizational chart.

content_en: Several project team members leave a project before it ends. To complete the current project, the project manager needs replacement team members from a new supplier but is concerned about controlling the cost. The project manager needs to work with the procurement team to establish specifications and the type of contract to be used. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Recommend a time and materials (T&M) contract.
option_2_content_en: Recommend a fixed-price-incentive-fee (FPIF) contract.
option_3_content_en: Recommend a cost-plus-incentive-fee (CPIF) contract.
option_4_content_en: Recommend a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract.

content_en: The project manager reviews a product backlog snapshot that includes feature priorities, estimated effort, expected value, and sustainability impact indicators. Recent market feedback shows declining value for several lower-priority features, while sustainability-related features demonstrate higher long-term benefits but require additional effort. Delivery capacity for the next iteration is constrained. Based on the backlog snapshot, what should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Reprioritize backlog items by value, effort, and sustainability impact before committing work.
option_2_content_en: Continue delivering backlog items in their current priority order to maintain delivery stability.
option_3_content_en: Remove sustainability-related features from the backlog to protect short-term delivery capacity.
option_4_content_en: Increase iteration scope to include all high-value items formally despite capacity constraints.

content_en: A project deliverable does not meet the agreed-upon quality specifications and is rejected by the customer. After an investigation, the project team finds a defect with the vendor-provided parts. This fault caused the issue, but the vendor says they cannot correct the situation. What should the project manager review before deciding on the next steps?
option_1_content_en: Service-level agreement (SLA) established with the vendor
option_2_content_en: Procurement management plan
option_3_content_en: Internal quality assurance reports
option_4_content_en: Contract agreements

content_en: A company initiates a project to meet a goal of increasing customer satisfaction within 4 months. The project manager needs to identify what the teams need to increase customer satisfaction. Which three methods should the project manager use to accomplish this goal? (Choose 3)
option_1_content_en: Surveys and questionnaires
option_2_content_en: Kano analysis
option_3_content_en: Product box exercise
option_4_content_en: Prototyping
option_5_content_en: Benchmarking

content_en: A company’s IT transformation project has three deliverables with the following characteristics: 1) Deliverable two has strictly scheduled milestones, with no expected variations in the timeline and scope requirements. 2) Requirements for deliverables one and three will change quickly during development. Which project approach should the project team use?
option_1_content_en: An agile approach with three product backlogs to control development
option_2_content_en: An agile approach with a single backlog for all three deliverables, prioritizing work by complexity to integrate continuous improvement
option_3_content_en: A hybrid approach with a fixed timeline, including an iterative development approach for deliverable two
option_4_content_en: A hybrid project model with an agile approach and a predictive development approach for deliverable two

content_en: An emergency vaccine distribution project should be deployed to vaccination centers as soon as confirmed locations are booked. Factors, such as delayed batch shipments, safety protocols, and target age groups, may block deployment at the last minute. Once the team is assured the risks will not materialize, deployment is straightforward. Which project approach would best support the goal of maximizing the number of vaccination centers deployed?
option_1_content_en: A predictive approach for deployment at each center to manage risks independently
option_2_content_en: Iterative deployments to each center within a predictive life cycle
option_3_content_en: A set of predictive deployment sequences with continuous improvement
option_4_content_en: A timeboxed agile life cycle with iterative deployments that contain the dependencies

content_en: A new wildlife preserve project will have a diverse staff of experts, builders, and logistics workers with exposure to various risks. These staff members want to share their learning for continuous improvement and define preferred ways of working while helping ensure agreed-on standards of safety. Which action should the staff use to tailor this type of project?
option_1_content_en: Utilize Crystal methods to design a scalable approach based on flexibility and teamwork.
option_2_content_en: Create and test models and process flow diagrams for team working scenarios.
option_3_content_en: Allow the experts to determine best practices and implement them incrementally.
option_4_content_en: Utilize a Six Sigma approach to refine quality control for high-risk processes.

content_en: A hybrid project is comprised of two teams: one production team and one programming team. During production, a 3D-printer malfunction causes a defect in the output. The production team informs the programming team about the issue, but the programming team claims they knew about the issue and resolved it. What should the team do to improve performance in the next iteration?
option_1_content_en: Publish risk register information on information radiators.
option_2_content_en: Ask the product owner to review product requirements.
option_3_content_en: Publish the team issue resolution process on information radiators.
option_4_content_en: Start regular daily coordination meetings with the two teams.

content_en: A medical equipment vendor is running a hybrid project that includes some custom software developed by an agile team. Team progress is good, but slow customer approval causes unnecessary delays. The customer insists that approval can only be given after repeating all the test cases in the target environment. What should the project manager do to accelerate the approvals and build customer trust at the same time?
option_1_content_en: Invite the customer to send representatives to observe team testing to preapprove the tests.
option_2_content_en: Coordinate with the customer to defer as many tests as possible to the final release.
option_3_content_en: Propose that team members work alongside the customer testers to run tests in their environment.
option_4_content_en: Allow the team to progress at their pace while the customer continues to test and approve earlier builds.

content_en: A project manager has documented internal resistance as a risk in an organization undergoing a transformation. The logistics team manager is particularly concerned about job losses in their department and the proposed rate of change. The logistics team manager formally requests a delay in the implementation of changes for the logistics team. What should the project manager do next in response to this request?
option_1_content_en: Work with the logistics team manager and transformation owner to reprioritize the backlog.
option_2_content_en: Conduct an impact analysis of the risk to the transformation project.
option_3_content_en: Perform a root cause analysis on the key factors causing the manager's resistance.
option_4_content_en: Review the risk register and implement the relevant risk response for the case.

content_en: A project team collected sensitive client data during the early stages of a project to help develop a project management plan. The team is working on deliverables for the project and the compliance manager discovers a data breach and alerts the team. Which document should the project manager update first?
option_1_content_en: Statement of work
option_2_content_en: Issue log
option_3_content_en: Quality management plan
option_4_content_en: Risk register

content_en: A project manager has completed the following steps: 1) Deployed a major IT system. 2) Confirmed with the release manager that all systems are working. 3) Confirmed that functionality has been verified by the quality assurance team. Which two additional steps should the project manager take to close the project or phase? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Move the lessons learned register to the lessons learned repository.
option_2_content_en: Update and close the risk register and issue log.
option_3_content_en: Review to confirm all contracts can be closed.
option_4_content_en: Finalize and release the release documentation.
option_5_content_en: Notify the project sponsor.

content_en: A project delivered a prototype as specified in the scope statement. The project team believes the quality of the prototype meets the required specifications. What should the project manager do next?

option_2_content_en: Seek stakeholder validation.
option_3_content_en: Verify the quality using the quality management plan.
option_4_content_en: Obtain formal approval from the client.

content_en: Project team members have been assigned to a project in the planning phase. Vendors have been engaged and contracts executed. Due to lack of funding, the project is suddenly terminated, and leadership instructs the project manager to close the project. What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Rely on the communications management plan to properly inform all stakeholders.
option_2_content_en: Examine the organization's project closure guidelines.
option_3_content_en: Perform a risk analysis to determine the potential impact of terminating the project.
option_4_content_en: Close all project procurement processes and open contracts.

content_en: A project team completes assigned development work on a project and the customer has accepted the deliverables. Despite project completion, the project manager and project team members are asked to evaluate new requirements and make some modifications. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Notify the customer that any further work will be considered a change request.
option_2_content_en: Review the acceptance criteria to make sure it was accurate.
option_3_content_en: Formally disband the project team and find a new project.
option_4_content_en: Put a fixed-price contract in place and fulfill the requests.

content_en: A complex project with high security protocols includes key stakeholders located in the United States, France, and China. A senior manager requests confidential project information to be shared with a third party. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Refer the request to the project management office (PMO) to decide if it is appropriate.
option_2_content_en: Supply the requested information but keep a record of the manager's request.
option_3_content_en: Supply the project information but help ensure the sensitive parts are redacted.
option_4_content_en: Check the communications management plan to verify the request is appropriate.

content_en: Due to a significant increase in project importance and complexity, a steering committee is appointed to work with a project sponsor. How should the project manager approach this change?
option_1_content_en: Assess the impact of the change in project governance and adjust the stakeholder engagement and communications management plans accordingly.
option_2_content_en: Follow the initial project management plan; recognize that the sponsor is the key stakeholder and the new committee members work at a lesser capacity.
option_3_content_en: Schedule an introductory meeting with the new steering committee and the project team, while continuing to follow the initial project management plan.
option_4_content_en: Help ensure the new steering committee members receive the current project status report.

content_en: In response to persistent delays on some scheduled tasks in a project, a project manager reprioritized several tasks to try to fix the problem. This approach did not work, so the project manager is escalating the issue. Which item should the project manager consult?
option_1_content_en: Change management plan
option_2_content_en: Stakeholder engagement assessment matrix
option_3_content_en: Communications management plan
option_4_content_en: Configuration management plan

content_en: An informal and unofficial blog was set up to enhance communication and morale among project team members. The project manager was not aware of the blog but has discovered that team members are using it. What should the project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Review the blog and assess the communications management plan.
option_2_content_en: Reprimand all individuals involved and report the issue to human resources.
option_3_content_en: Close the blog because it is not a necessary part of the project.
option_4_content_en: Remind the team about the ground rules in the team charter.

content_en: A project owner is developing a customer service prototype for the marketing department in a company. The customer stakeholder group includes franchise owners and direct customers of the company. The prototype scores 95% on fulfillment of the functional requirements defined in the scope, which is a passing score in the project’s agreed-upon quality metrics. The franchise group is unwilling to approve the prototype because it does not fulfill a particular functional requirement, but the direct customer group approves. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Review the specific feedback from both stakeholder groups on the prototype in the documentation from product demos.
option_2_content_en: Engage the franchise group, review the acceptance criteria, and discuss the specific requirement they need fulfilled to obtain approval.
option_3_content_en: Consult with the franchise group, show them the direct customer approval, and negotiate for the validation.
option_4_content_en: Revisit and update the requirements in the statement of work.

The project manager hires more team members for the production of the application. Which risk response strategy does this scenario exemplify?
option_1_content_en: Mitigate
option_2_content_en: Transfer
option_3_content_en: Accept
option_4_content_en: Avoid

content_en: While implementing a product design, a project team realizes the packaging might not meet the requirements when the product is shipped overseas. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Perform a qualitative risk analysis.
option_2_content_en: Enter the issue in the issue log and submit a change request.
option_3_content_en: Ask the stakeholders what they would like to do.
option_4_content_en: Contact a potentially affected customer, run a simulation, and negotiate for risk acceptance.

content_en: A company is planning a project in a remote area with limited access to transportation and equipment. Additionally, the government is requiring the company to sign a contract to protect the environment and road from damage, because the road to the site goes through a protected area. The project manager determines the preferred way to manage this risk is to subcontract delivery to a specialized firm, despite the significant added expense. What type of risk response is the project manager demonstrating?
option_1_content_en: Transfer
option_2_content_en: Outsource
option_3_content_en: Accept
option_4_content_en: Avoid

content_en: A project is being implemented in a company. The research and development department communicates to the project manager that new and better technology is available and product requirements might change. These changes were not anticipated and may significantly influence scope and quality. Which action should the project manager take next?
option_1_content_en: Review the risk management plan to understand and identify risk responses.
option_2_content_en: Use the contingency reserve to pay for the change and get project sponsor approval.
option_3_content_en: Review the requirements traceability matrix to verify the product functionality requirements.
option_4_content_en: Ask the research and development department to submit a change request.

content_en: Match each governance element with its primary purpose.
option_1_content_en:
(1)	
Performance Tolerances
option_1_match_en: Specify when issues or risks must be escalated for higher-level attention
option_2_content_en:

Decision Authority Matrix
option_2_match_en: Identify who has authority to approve specific decisions
option_3_content_en:

Governance Review Board
option_3_match_en: Provide oversight and approval for significant project decisions
option_4_content_en:

content_en: A project team working on a large, on-site infrastructure project on-site brings a potentially significant risk to the project manager’s attention. The project manager wants more information before presenting the new risk information and a solution to the steering committee and stakeholders. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Prepare a risk report on the risks using the information from the project team.
option_2_content_en: Verify the risk was identified in the risk register.
option_3_content_en: Consult the stakeholder engagement plan and update the issue log.
option_4_content_en: Perform a Monte Carlo analysis.

content_en: The project manager reviews a risk register excerpt highlighting several active risks. One risk related to supplier sustainability compliance has recently increased in probability due to changes in supplier practices. The risk response strategy currently defined is “monitor,” with escalation thresholds based on impact to cost, schedule, and reputational risk. Based on the information in the risk register, what should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Remove the risk from active tracking since no direct schedule impact has occurred.
option_2_content_en: Continue monitoring the risk closely until escalation thresholds are formally breached.
option_3_content_en: Reassess the risk response and update mitigation actions based on increased probability.
option_4_content_en: Transfer ownership of the risk to the procurement team to avoid project-level exposure.

content_en: An international space project requires a project team composed of teams in four different locations around the globe. Two teams must be working round the clock. Which document should the project manager modify first?
option_1_content_en: Team charter
option_2_content_en: Resource calendar
option_3_content_en: Project management plan
option_4_content_en: Resource management plan

content_en: A project manager implemented an approved change to manage a risk in a project. Three months after the implemented change, the project manager learns the change did not produce the desired result, instead producing negative consequences. What should the project manager do to avoid this problem in future projects?
option_1_content_en: Revisit the probability and impact matrix after assessing any new risks.
option_2_content_en: Assign a risk owner to each identified risk.
option_3_content_en: Update the lessons learned register with the risk information.
option_4_content_en: Update all risks in the risk register with secondary and residual risk information.

content_en: A retiring project manager hands over all materials for a project to a new project manager. The project appears to be running smoothly, until a critical component fails during testing. What should the new project manager do first?
option_1_content_en: Review the risk management plan to verify this risk and accompanying response strategies have been captured.
option_2_content_en: Log the issue in the issue log, then work with the project team to respond to the issue.
option_3_content_en: Revise the timeline to account for slippage due to the additional time needed to implement mitigation.
option_4_content_en: Communicate with stakeholders by describing the issue, proposed costs, and potential changes related to the project delivery dates.

content_en: The technical lead of a project team wants to take unplanned leave during the execution of a project. Taking unplanned leave will cause disruption, posing a risk to the delivery schedule. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Assess the risk with the project team.
option_2_content_en: Review the resource management plan for project team member skills.
option_3_content_en: Revisit the schedule and adjust the timeline.
option_4_content_en: Document the risk in the issue log.

content_en: A major city and a national government agency are partnering on a new project. Each of these entities has a different risk threshold. It is the project manager’s role to help ensure a risk approach that will satisfy both parties. What should the project manager do next to accomplish this?
option_1_content_en: Focus on completing the work according to the schedule in the project management plan.
option_2_content_en: Ask the city sponsor for additional contingency reserve to cover risk planning.
option_3_content_en: Work with representatives from both sides of the partnership to develop a risk management plan.
option_4_content_en: List and assess any project risks and present them to the city sponsor.

content_en: After the start of a project, a project manager learns that an expected governmental subsidy might not be available. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Log the risk.
option_2_content_en: Log the issue.
option_3_content_en: Help ensure sufficient funds in the contingency reserve.
option_4_content_en: Make a change request.

content_en: To speed up completion of a mining project, a project team needs to work a full 24-hour day, in three shifts, and in hazardous conditions. Team A: 02:00 – 10:00, Team B: 10:00 – 18:00, Team C: 18:00 – 02:00. To safely work nighttime hours, teams A and C will need to receive overtime pay. The company will also need to increase security measures and insurance coverage. How should the project manager plan for the risks associated with project team conditions?
option_1_content_en: Include all the risk details in the risk management plan.
option_2_content_en: Identify and assess the risks in the risk register.
option_3_content_en: Work with the organization for additional funding.
option_4_content_en: Record the risk conditions and provisions in the team charter.

content_en: A project manager realizes stakeholder interests will conflict on a project and decides to utilize a stakeholder engagement assessment matrix. The matrix pinpoints an influential stakeholder resistant to the project. The project manager needs to align this stakeholder's expectations with the goals of the project. What should the project manager do to accomplish this goal?
option_1_content_en: Consult the stakeholder engagement plan and engage the resistant stakeholder accordingly.
option_2_content_en: Have one-on-one conversations with the resistant stakeholder.
option_3_content_en: Gain consensus on project objectives by meeting with all stakeholders.
option_4_content_en: Develop a workaround for the resistant stakeholder.

content_en: How can a project manager gain a stakeholder’s approval if the stakeholder believes a project's deliverables did not meet expectations?
option_1_content_en: Review the acceptance criteria and benefits realization plan with the stakeholder.
option_2_content_en: Review the project charter thoroughly with this stakeholder and negotiate a positive outcome.
option_3_content_en: Help ensure the stakeholder understands the quality management plan.
option_4_content_en: Explain to the stakeholder that the project requirements were fulfilled in the deliverables scope and the deliverables were validated.

content_en: A project is nearly complete, and a project manager learns a key stakeholder is ill and needs to decrease their level of involvement. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Update the stakeholder register and stakeholder engagement plan.
option_2_content_en: Revise the project charter with the updated stakeholder information.
option_3_content_en: Ask the project sponsor to replace the stakeholder.
option_4_content_en: Update the stakeholder engagement plan.

content_en: A project manager is creating an agenda and presentation materials for a kickoff meeting that will involve stakeholders across the globe.  How should the project manager facilitate and optimize stakeholder engagement for the kickoff meeting?
option_1_content_en: Allow stakeholders to help plan the meeting.
option_2_content_en: Coordinate with stakeholders to accommodate the teams in different time zones.
option_3_content_en: Arrange for the meeting to be recorded for viewing after the meeting.
option_4_content_en: Remind stakeholders that meeting attendance is mandatory.

content_en: Six different companies are involved in a project. The project sponsor is the board of directors of a global organization and there are more than 50 named stakeholders. Midpoint in the project, the project manager learns that one stakeholder is experiencing difficulties and cannot provide their expected level of involvement. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Consult the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix.
option_2_content_en: Consider the impact of this stakeholder's engagement on the project.
option_3_content_en: Update the stakeholder register and stakeholder engagement plan.
option_4_content_en: Remove the stakeholder and update the stakeholder engagement plan.

The project manager reviews a financial summary combined with a benefits tracking view. The summary shows that actual costs are trending slightly above plan due to sustainability-related initiatives, while projected long-term benefits remain aligned with the business case. Short-term cost variance is within tolerance, but contingency reserves are decreasing faster than expected. Sponsors are concerned about near-term financial optics, while the business case emphasizes long-term value realization.

Based on the financial summary and benefits tracking information, what should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Reassess spending decisions by balancing short-term cost variance against long-term benefits and value realization.
option_2_content_en: Reduce or pause sustainability-related initiatives to stabilize short-term cost performance.
option_3_content_en: Continue current spending without adjustment since projected benefits remain aligned with the business case.
option_4_content_en: Escalate the cost variance to governance and request an immediate budget increase.

content_en: The product owner is part of a project team working on an adaptive project. Team members complain there are too many meetings and not enough time for project work. What should this team do to adjust their way of working?
option_1_content_en: Raise "too many meetings" as an impediment in the daily coordination meetings.
option_2_content_en: Reevaluate team member responsibilities and emphasize meeting attendance for responsible roles only.
option_3_content_en: Make daily coordination meetings optional for the product owner and apply timeboxes to other meetings.
option_4_content_en: Ask the product owner to explain the value of meetings as essential to getting project work done.

content_en: A deliverable on the critical path of a project is behind schedule. The cost performance index (CPI) is 1.3. The project manager would like to use fast-tracking to get the project back on schedule. Which three results are the most likely for this project?  (Choose 3)
option_1_content_en: Activities will be performed in parallel.
option_2_content_en: Project scope will be revised.
option_3_content_en: Associated risks will increase.
option_4_content_en: Costs will increase.
option_5_content_en: The team should expect rework.

content_en: The per story cost in an agile project has risen by more than 250% over the past 6 months due to a faulty platform that is no longer supported. The work will exceed the budget increment threshold in the next iteration. Who should decide if the work should be canceled?
option_1_content_en: Product manager
option_2_content_en: Product owner
option_3_content_en: Procurement manager
option_4_content_en: Project manager

content_en: A project has the following characteristics: 1) There are three main tasks. 2) Task A must be delivered 4 weeks before task C starts. 3)  Once task B is finished, task C will start. What is the relationship between tasks A and B?
option_1_content_en: Finish-to-start
option_2_content_en: Finish-to-finish
option_3_content_en: Start-to-start
option_4_content_en: Start-to-finish

content_en: A company is planning to utilize a new product that leverages innovative technologies and processes. The project manager has verified that the component work packages have been defined and constraints for each component have been identified. Which estimating technique should the project manager use to obtain a precise cost estimate of the project?
option_1_content_en: Analogous
option_2_content_en: Three-point
option_3_content_en: Bottom-up
option_4_content_en: Parametric

content_en: A project manager is uncertain about the duration of a project for a new product and consults six groups of subject matter experts. The first group advises that development can be finished in 40 days. The second group identifies some risks that could lengthen the duration by up to 60 days. The third group proposes a new development optimistically shortening the time to 20 days. The fourth, fifth, and sixth groups all estimated the work to be finished in 40 days. What estimating approach is likely to yield the most accurate estimate?
option_1_content_en: Three-point estimating
option_2_content_en: Weighted three-point estimating
option_3_content_en: Analogous estimating
option_4_content_en: Rough order of magnitude

content_en: A project manager is uncertain about the duration of a new project and consults with several groups. The first group advises that development can be finished in 29 days. The second group identifies some risks that could increase the duration by up to 46 days. The third group proposes a new development method that can shorten the time to 18 days. Using the triangular estimation technique, what is the estimated development duration for the new product?
option_1_content_en: 28 days
option_2_content_en: 31 days
option_3_content_en: 32 days
option_4_content_en: 36 days

content_en: A project manager is uncertain about the duration of a new product development project and consults with several groups of subject matter experts (SMEs). The first group advises that development can be finished in 14 days. The second group identifies some risks that could lengthen the duration by up to 32 days. The third group proposes a new development method that can shorten the time to 8 days. What is the estimated development duration for the new product using the program evaluation and review technique (PERT)?
option_1_content_en: 12 days
option_2_content_en: 16 days
option_3_content_en: 14 days
option_4_content_en: 20 days

content_en: A trend of stories is incomplete, which becomes apparent at the end of several iterations. The team worked on these stories and no blockers were identified. What should the agile team do to resolve this issue?
option_1_content_en: Put the stories back into the product backlog and wait for a less intensive iteration to work on them.
option_2_content_en: Use the next iteration for a team spike to determine the feasibility of completing the stories.
option_3_content_en: Increase the number of iterations for story completion and work with the product owner to remove impediments.
option_4_content_en: Work with the product owner to further break down the stories in the backlog and update the definition of ready (DoR).

content_en: The executive sponsor of an agile project is concerned because the last four project schedule reports showed significant fluctuations in the projected completion date. What should the team do to forecast the projected completion date with more accuracy and certainty?
option_1_content_en: Help ensure upcoming backlog items are elaborated in more detail with the team.
option_2_content_en: Address impediments more proactively.
option_3_content_en: Plan for varying iteration sizes according to story complexity and load.
option_4_content_en: Explain the schedule deviations to the executive stakeholders.

content_en: An IT integration team experienced a major failure after a third-party software company deployed a security patch that caused new software to fail. Which two actions should the project team take next? (Choose 2)
option_1_content_en: Meet with the scrum master to determine if the product vision is still valid.
option_2_content_en: Meet with the product owner to update the product backlog during the iteration.
option_3_content_en: Conduct an impact analysis and consult the risk register for the response.
option_4_content_en: Log the defect in the impediment log and perform a root cause analysis.
option_5_content_en: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor.

content_en: A skincare company is updating their product packaging. During testing, the quality test team observes the product is changing color, depending on storage and heat conditions. Which tool or technique should the project manager use to determine the problem?
option_1_content_en: Scatter diagram
option_2_content_en: Affinity diagram
option_3_content_en: Root cause analysis
option_4_content_en: Control chart

Case Study 2: Digital Product Delivery Under Market Pressure
A large organization is developing a customer-facing digital product intended to replace several fragmented legacy solutions used by its customers across multiple regions. The initiative is strategically important due to increasing customer churn and competitive pressure from digital-native competitors that offer faster, more personalized experiences. Executive leadership expects the product to improve customer satisfaction, increase operational transparency, and enable quicker responses to changing market demands.

You are assigned as the project manager after initial funding is approved. The product scope is defined at a high level, with clear business objectives, but detailed requirements are expected to evolve based on customer feedback and regulatory considerations related to data privacy and service availability. Some teams advocate for a highly adaptive delivery approach to accelerate learning and respond quickly to feedback, while others emphasize the need for more structure to manage dependencies, compliance constraints, and integration with existing enterprise systems.

As planning progresses, multiple delivery teams become involved, including software development, data analytics, operations, and customer support. Coordination proves challenging due to different delivery cadences, varying levels of agile maturity, and competing operational priorities. While initial planning artifacts exist, there is limited agreement on how progress and forecasts should be communicated to leadership in a way that reflects not only task completion but also value delivered to customers.
Midway through execution, leadership requests more frequent and data-driven visibility into delivery progress and expected release timelines after a key competitor announces a similar product enhancement. Teams express concern that estimates remain uncertain because requirements continue to evolve and technical complexity is higher than anticipated. Discussions emerge about using advanced analytical tools to support forecasting and provide insights, while emphasizing that final decisions and accountability must remain with project leadership.

As the product approaches a major release milestone, several critical impediments surface, including integration delays and performance risks that could impact customer experience at launch. External changes in customer expectations further complicate prioritization decisions. The project team must determine how to address these impediments, reassess delivery expectations, and maintain stakeholder trust while continuing to focus on delivering meaningful value.

In the later stages of the initiative, portions of the product are released incrementally, generating early usage data and customer feedback. Leadership looks to the project manager to help interpret this information, guide trade-off decisions, and ensure that ongoing delivery choices remain aligned with strategic objectives, regulatory obligations, and long-term value realization rather than short-term visibility alone.

At the start of the initiative, leadership expects early visibility into delivery progress and release forecasts, while detailed requirements are expected to evolve due to customer feedback, regulatory considerations, and market pressure. Teams express concern that committing too early could reduce adaptability, but leadership remains focused on predictability and confidence. What should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Establish value-based prioritization criteria to guide delivery and forecasting as requirements evolve.
option_2_content_en: Commit to a fixed delivery plan early to provide leadership with reliable timelines and increase confidence.
option_3_content_en: Delay forecasting and reporting until requirements stabilize to avoid providing misleading information.
option_4_content_en: Allow delivery teams to self-organize delivery decisions without defining common prioritization guidance.
